chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem ibn Ibrahim, from Abbad al-Basri, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about three men who testified against a man for adultery, and they said, 'We will now bring the fourth.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are whipped with the penalty of the slanderer, eighty lashes, each man among them.'

key_terms.الْقَاذِفِ: The slanderer (one who accuses of zina without four witnesses)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for three witnesses who testify to adultery but wait for a fourth witness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'ta'abbun' (approximation) in Shia jurisprudence, where the three witnesses are penalized for slander because the fourth witness has not yet materialized to complete the required four. It highlights the rigorous evidentiary standards for hadd al-zina, ensuring that partial testimony does not suffice for full conviction but triggers the penalty for the accusers. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on procedural justice and the protection of individuals from premature legal consequences.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem Bin Ibrahim, from Abbad Al basry who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about three testimonies upon a man, with the adultery, and they said, ‘We will now be coming with the fourth’. Heasws said: ‘They would be whipped with the Penalty (Hadd) of the slander, eighty lashes, each man among them’.
